::: {#rem-expectation-long-run-average}
#### The expectation is the long-run average of repeated draws

The [weak law of large numbers](#thm-wlln)
gives the [expectation](expectation.qmd#def-expectation) a second reading.
Draw $X_1, X_2, \ldots$ independently
from the [distribution](random-variables.qmd#def-cdf) of $X$,
so that they are [IID](independence.qmd#def-iid)
with [population mean](expectation.qmd#def-expectation) $\E{X}$.
The [sample mean](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/linear-algebra-vectors.html#def-mean) of the first $n$ draws
then [converges in probability](#def-convergence-in-probability) to $\E{X}$:
for a large $n$,
the [average](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/linear-algebra-vectors.html#def-mean) of the draws
is very probably close to $\E{X}$.
So the expectation is the value
that the average of many repeated draws settles near.

For a [finite](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/functions.html#def-finite-set) population,
the two readings agree.
[The population-mean proposition](expectation.qmd#prp-population-mean-expectation)
shows that $\E{X}$ is the average over the whole population
when $X$ is the value of one unit [chosen at random](probability-basics.qmd#def-random-choice).
Units drawn [at random](probability-basics.qmd#def-random-choice) with replacement are IID,
so the average over many draws settles near that population average.

:::
